subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow stale OpenAI session-route repair, folded into the broader #87957 shared resolver, or treated as expected behavior for explicit `/model openai` sessions with better diagnostics?
rationale: Source inspection shows DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the report mixes plugin hot reload, persisted OpenAI selected state, and an explicit manual model switch, so automation should not choose the durable session-state contract.

options.title: Fix narrow stale route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI/Codex session state for non-OpenAI primaries while preserving explicit `/model openai` choices and keep #87957 for the broader resolver.

options.title: Fold into #87957
options.body: Use #87957 as the canonical owner and copy this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload case into its acceptance criteria before closing this issue later.

options.title: Keep explicit OpenAI behavior
options.body: If maintainers decide the report is only an explicit `/model openai` session, keep Codex-for-OpenAI behavior and improve status or doctor messaging instead of changing routing.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow stale route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI/Codex session state for non-OpenAI primaries while preserving explicit `/model openai` choices and keep #87957 for the broader resolver.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-history signal across the Codex/OpenAI runtime policy and session model resolver surfaces involved in this choice.
